design.closureSource: An accepted normal humanagent_turn_end tool call followed by actual producer drain/settle has source agent-tool. Watchdog, permission, steer and stop retain their typed harness-control source and settle evidence; genuine recovery closure retains recovery. Historical retained intents, frozen inputs and preparations keep their original source. App execution-composition.ts supplies the normal close input and reads the committed canonical closure source for the native save intent; native-execution.ts passes the frozen close source or intent.closure.source into the existing preparation seam. Runtime remains the checkpoint/control owner and JSONL remains the Journal writer. Binding schema and core node owners are unchanged.
design.closingOutcome: The first live closing checkpoint outcome is computed once from the actual owners: an accepted standard end and a real producer drain are required before any outcome other than unknown; unreturned request/child-invocation refs and unresolved operation refs keep unknown; revoked permission or any hard blocker keeps blocked; a failed or cancelled settle keeps that state; an accepted end with a first error retains waiting; only a drained, accepted, granted standard turn with no unresolved responsibility freezes succeeded. frozen.inputs is the historical recovery entry and its stored outcome is returned unchanged, so an older waiting close is never rewritten to succeeded by newer live facts. The app owner of this decision is execution-owner-facts.ts; occurrence-terminal consumers, runner SETTLE_TERMINAL_STATES and domain terminal criteria are unchanged.
design.reviewAcceptanceOrder: settle() reports the settlement value only. The first closing checkpoint is cut and committed atomically by the first canonical close read, which happens after the orchestration dispatch owner has accepted its completed review receipts. dispatch reviews accepted after the closing cut are rejected instead of rewriting the frozen closure.
design.singleWriter: Runtime Checkpoint/Control Owner submits typed intents; the JSONL Journal Owner alone appends, assigns sequence/digest, flushes, and returns durable receipts.
design.stageEnvelope: Expected phase errors and unknown results are values in the typed envelope, not Operator transport failures. A durable phase may execute a side effect only when its incoming envelope declares its exact prerequisite phase succeeded, the commit identity is unchanged, and permission/epoch checks pass; otherwise it emits not-executed with the original first error/cause and recovery ref. Following nodes are still scheduled in this static DAG, but must not perform their side effect when gated off. Both recovery projections always run as pure transformations: auto_resume_same_turn_segment is active only when all five durable phases have eligible receipts and no unknown mutating effect; enter_recovery_hold is active for any failed/unknown/not-executed phase, missing receipt, stale epoch, unresolved operation, or unknown mutating effect. The unique Z verifies exactly one active projection and returns all recorded facts.
design.routingEvidence: DAGpipe 0.1.1 installed SDK Edge has only from/to/arc_id; its executor schedules all nodes in each topological wave. No conditional-edge or mutually exclusive route support is evidenced. This graph is target topology and envelope contract only; conditional activation and effect gating require future runtime implementation/evidence.
design.historyQualification: History publication requires committed checkpoint, committed closure, and committed Context View receipts. Publication itself is not turn closure and does not grant next-turn eligibility.
design.rawRetention: Preserve current-turn raw evidence until a complete durable turn receipt is returned. Never delete immutable Journal facts or evidence assets.
design.idempotency: Retries use the same commit identity and return the original durable fact and timestamp; they do not invent a later time.
design.operatorStatus: Bindings identify responsibility paths only. No Operator registration, static type validation, runtime behavior, or product acceptance is claimed.
